title: Pentagon plans to hold report on Iran school strike past November midterms
key_facts: Top Pentagon officials intend to hold an internal report on the attack on a school in Minab, southern Iran, until after the US midterm elections at the earliest, per anonymous sources.
Advisers to Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth have told some Pentagon personnel of the plan; no final decision on the timeline has been made.
On the first day of the war, US air strikes on Shajarah Tayyebeh Elementary School killed more than 150 people, including at least 123 children.

An earlier Bloomberg News investigation found flawed intelligence, outdated imagery and over-reliance on AI contributed to the attack; the probe began in March and the report is said to be all but complete.
A Pentagon official said the investigation is ongoing with "no updates to announce at this time".
Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, a New York Democrat on the Senate armed services panel, called the delay "disgraceful".
The House defence bill would require the final report within 30 days of completion; the Senate draft has similar language; more than 70 Democratic lawmakers wrote to Hegseth on 8 Oct.
quote_evidence: Top Pentagon officials have expressed their intention to hold off on releasing an internal report into the attack on a school in southern Iran until after the US midterm elections at the earliest, according to sources familiar with the matter.
No final decisions have been made on the precise timeline for disclosing any details from the Minab report.
why_it_matters_hint: Transparency about the deadliest US targeting error of the century, in which AI over-reliance reportedly played a part.
notes: Straits Times carries Bloomberg text (ends "BLOOMBERG"); credited to Bloomberg. Anonymous sources.
